Casablanca-born · Regraga-rooted · KAUST TIE target · Saudi Vision 2030 alignment

From Casablanca Roots to Cognitive Cities: A Smart-City Investment Scorecard for Vision 2030.

This portfolio connects my Casablanca-based research foundation with a Saudi-facing AI decision framework. It brings together Regraga cultural memory, bilingual design, AI-MCDA logic, PFE evidence, KAUST TIE venture thinking, and an Amanah evidence system. Guided by Ihsan and Al-Amānah, it translates empirical traffic simulation, GIS, CAPEX/OPEX modelling, machine learning validation, and venture-readiness logic into an auditable decision engine for smart-city infrastructure.

🛡️ Fully Auditable: TRIPOD+AI & PROBAST+AI-informed reporting boundaries 🌍 Culturally Native: Selective RTL mirroring & WCAG-oriented accessibility 📈 Vision 2030 Aligned: Smart City infrastructure & Circular Carbon Economy (CCE) 📊 Empirically Grounded: PFE + SUMO/GIS + CAPEX/OPEX evidence base 🌿 SGI / Net Zero 2060 lens active: carbon, CCE, and mitigation-ready assets are foregrounded.

03 — Urban Intelligence

Casablanca DOOH Profitability: An Empirical Smart-City Evidence Case.

This page demonstrates foundational urban intelligence and financial engineering. By triangulating microscopic traffic simulation (SUMO), spatial mapping (GIS), and rigorous CAPEX/OPEX modeling, I developed an auditable decision-support framework to maximize infrastructure ROI.

OOH Mode · Lower CAPEX, static exposure, accelerated break-even.

Smart City Data-Toggle

Traditional OOH emphasizes low technical complexity and minimal capital expenditure (CAPEX). It offers fast break-even logic (approx. 5.2 weeks) for mass-coverage zones where digital premiums are not yet justified.

SUMOGISCAPEX/OPEX/TCOIRP
01Problem framingIdentifying the gap between urban traffic density and infrastructure ROI under strict regulatory constraints.
02SUMO simulationDeploying Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) to microscopically model vehicle and pedestrian flows across peak and off-peak intervals.
03GIS mappingLayering spatial zones to correlate traffic intensity with local purchasing-power proxies and urban harmony rules.
04Financial modelingStructuring CAPEX and OPEX parameters to calculate Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) and operational break-even thresholds.
05Potential index (IRP)Formulating the Potential Profitability Index (IRP) from 15+ variables to rank locations based on long-term value creation.
06Scenario testingComparing financial viability across OOH Secondary, OOH Premium, DOOH Secondary, and DOOH Premium asset classes.
07Regulatory filterIntegrating municipal guidelines as hard feasibility constraints, anticipating smart-city compliance requirements.
08Decision outputSynthesizing data into a structured investment recommendation matrix, supporting executive capital allocation.

04 — Decision Engine

Decision Engine: Smart City Capital Allocation.

This section moves from predictive forecasting to strategic ranking. It integrates XGBoost demand predictions with carbon-adjusted Decoupled Net Present Value (DNPV) and AROMAN ranking to prioritize Vision 2030 infrastructure investments under geoeconomic and climate uncertainty. Multi-criteria scorecards improve reviewability compared with a single-indicator NPV model.

Layer 1 · Macro-Environmental Risk

Energy scenarios, EU ETS carbon-cost exposure (€0 to €150/tCO₂), and Geopolitical Risk (GPR) indices.

Layer 2 · AI Prediction

XGBoost demand forecasting. Capability indicator: 45.8% Mean Absolute Error (MAE) reduction compared to Ridge regression baselines.

Layer 3 · Valuation & Weighting

Carbon-adjusted DNPV and Real Options Valuation combined with hybrid Fuzzy-AHP/MEREC weighting.

Layer 4 · AROMAN Ranking

Cross-validated against TOPSIS and COPRAS. AROMAN diverged from NPV-only rankings across all 25 tested projects.

SGI / Net Zero 2060 lens

Why this mode exists

SGI Mode does not simply recolor the interface. It applies a Saudi Green Initiative lens that foregrounds carbon exposure, Circular Carbon Economy logic, and green-infrastructure resilience so the ranking behaves like a policy-aware decision interface.

Carbon indicatorsHigher carbon-price pathways become more visible and ranking stress becomes easier to read.
Circular Carbon EconomyMitigation-ready and efficiency-oriented projects receive clearer visual and analytical emphasis.
Net Zero 2060 lensThe interface explicitly signals when the portfolio is being read through Saudi Green Initiative priorities.
Why it mattersThe policy lens changes the ranking logic without hiding the original baseline evidence.
CCE note: this mode does not replace financial discipline; it adds carbon resilience and mitigation value to the investment logic.

The Vision 2030 Stress-Test Lab (AROMAN & Carbon)

This mini-dashboard demonstrates model transparency: rankings shift when normative trade-offs or carbon-price scenarios change.

0.3 = Cost-minimization · 0.7 = Benefit-maximization

05 — Vision 2030 Agenda

Vision 2030 Agenda: A Venture-Readiness Roadmap for Saudi Cognitive Cities.

Transitioning completed empirical research (PFE) and advanced AI methodologies (MSc) into a commercializable decision-support framework. This roadmap aims to optimize smart mobility and infrastructure investments for Saudi megaprojects, bridging technical feasibility with institutional trust.

G

Gap

AI mobility concepts often fail commercialization if they ignore data sovereignty and institutional trust. Current models partially capture the rigorous compliance costs required by the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) and SDAIA governance mandates.

I

Idea

A venture-ready AI-MCDA framework linking mobility value and predictive AI with transparent model reporting. It transforms urban data into risk-adjusted investment decisions for Vision 2030 megaprojects.

F

Feasibility

Grounded in design science and lean startup logic. Feasibility is ensured through synthetic mobility scenario modelling (SUMO), strict regulatory mapping (NDMO frameworks), and TRIPOD+AI-informed transparent model validation.

T

Timeline

A 36-to-48 month execution trajectory. A staged path from regulatory mapping and MVP specification to synthetic scenario validation for cognitive cities.

KAUST TIE Gantt · Product-Oriented Research Trajectory

Y1 · Sovereign Governance & ArchitectureMapping SDAIA / NDMO compliance boundaries for data ingestion.
Y1–Y2 · Predictive AI Mobility EngineXGBoost/MCDA algorithms using synthetic and aggregated open-source data.
Y2 · Prototype & MVP DashboardUser-centric dashboard for auditability and sensitivity disclosure.
Y2–Y3 · Megaproject Scenario ValidationSynthetic adaptation to Riyadh Metro or NEOM's The Line; CCE variables.
Y3 · Commercialization & Venture ReadinessCustomer discovery, Lean startup validation, PIF/VRP alignment logic.
Y3–Y4 · Institutional TransferAcademic output and handover of venture-readiness framework.
Scientific Prudence & Deployment Boundaries (Al-Amānah). In line with Al-Amānah (intellectual integrity and trustworthiness), this proposal clarifies its scope. The project is a prototype-level venture-readiness framework and an MVP specification. It relies on synthetic scenario modelling and does not represent operational deployment or live data integration within NEOM, Riyadh Metro, or any Saudi municipality. Formal institutional data access remains a prerequisite for transitioning this academic framework into a prescriptive, deployed platform.

System Architecture

System Architecture & Interactive Governance.

This portfolio is structured as a venture-ready decision interface. Interactive features are designed to support algorithmic transparency, cultural localization for the MENA region, and international AI reporting standards.

🌍 Pillar 1 : Vision 2030 & Cultural Localization

  • SGI Mode: More than a color theme; visually aligns the interface with Circular Carbon Economy objectives.
  • Selective RTL Mirroring: English-to-Arabic UI transition while maintaining universal data visualizations.
  • Smart City Data-Toggle: OOH / DOOH / Hybrid comparison for low-CAPEX legacy assets and high-ROI digital assets.

🛡️ Pillar 2 : Algorithmic Transparency & Al-Amānah

  • Normative Sensitivity Lab: λ trade-off slider showing cost-minimization vs. benefit-maximization.
  • Epistemic Scope & Evidence: terms such as supported, partially validated, scenario transfer, and implementation limits.
  • Institutional Sources & Evidence: traceability of geoeconomic, regulatory, and demographic inputs.

🔒 Pillar 3 : The Evidence Archive

  • Document Access: central download links for the PFE, Final Paper, KAUST SOP, and Venture Research Proposal.
  • One-Click APA Citation Engine: academic referencing for the Final Paper replication package.
  • Leaflet/SUMO Traffic Dashboard: heatmap and real-time vehicle simulation engine from the project portfolio.
  • Sticky Global Navigation: transition from local urban data to global AI strategy.
